statement.text:
Given a complex irreducible character χ ∈ Irr(G) of a finite group G, let Q(χ)
denote the field extension of Q obtained by adjoining to Q all the values of χ. We say
that a finite group G is k-rational if |Q(χ) : Q| divides k for every χ ∈ Irr(G). Does
there exist a real-valued function f such that if p is the order of a cyclic composition
factor of a k-rational group G, then p ⩽ f (k)?
    If k = 1, then we know that p ⩽ 11 by a theorem of J. G. Thompson (J. Algebra,
319 (2008), 558–594).                                                          A. Moretó
